A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GVDepth with the same core method and experiments. Their complete main texts, supplementary materials, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-estimation experiments across five driving datasets, including representation ablations, calibration experiments, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds surround-camera evaluation and expanded ground-plane method comparisons.

M1.justification: The canonical depth transformations, two-branch architecture, uncertainty-weighted fusion, losses, geometric augmentations, and calibration algorithm remain unchanged. Revised geometry exposition and reduced decoder documentation do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The five datasets and depth-estimation task remain. v2 extends frontal-camera coverage with Waymo surround images for training and DDAD side/rear-camera evaluation in Table 4, introducing additional viewing and occlusion conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds a supervised PlaneDepth variant to the ground-plane comparison and adds GEDepth to the semantic-class comparison in Figure 6. GEDepth, ordinary PlaneDepth, and GroCo already appeared in v1; their expanded tables do not constitute newly introduced baseline methods.

E3.justification: Ground-plane comparisons gain substantial experimental controls: GEDepth is evaluated under matched training settings and model complexity, and PlaneDepth is additionally trained with supervision using GVDepth's backbone. v2 also introduces frontal-only versus surround-image training for surround-camera testing. Existing benchmark splits and training budgets remain; the stated metric list drops Sq.Rel.

E4.justification: v2 adds surround-view transfer and training-coverage ablations, extends semantic-class error analysis to GEDepth, and reports GEDepth attention-collapse and convergence failures. The resolution-adaptability, fusion, ground-perturbation, and calibration-sensitivity analyses already existed in v1 and are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix G newly reports adequate GEDepth ground-attention convergence only on the 19th training experiment. This adds limited information about repeated training attempts, without establishing identical settings across attempts or adding seeds, confidence intervals, or aggregate run statistics.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1 and 3 retain their results, while v2 adds surround-view scores, extensive GEDepth comparisons, and supervised PlaneDepth results. KITTI-to-DDAD GEDepth A.Rel changes from the cited 26.1 in v1 to 19.46 under v2's matched-training evaluation, not a demonstrated same-setting improvement. Ordinary PlaneDepth RMS changes from 14.0 in v1 Table 2 to 14.77 in v2 Table 6.

T1.justification: Section 3 revises the coordinate formulation and replaces v1's incomplete ground-plane expression with an equation containing the point variable and an explicit ray-plane derivation. The resulting scalar depth mapping is unchanged. Appendix G adds mathematical analysis of ground-attention mixtures and their disentanglement properties.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central canonical-representation, probabilistic-fusion, and single-dataset generalization claims. The introduction drops v1's explicit claim of being first to achieve accurate single-camera-trained out-of-distribution estimation and explicitly highlights training scalability in its new contribution list.

C2.justification: Appendix G substantially expands explanations attributing competing methods' weaknesses to ground-attention mixtures and incomplete perspective disentanglement. v2 adds a rear-camera occlusion hypothesis and discusses implicit adaptation to imperfect ground planes and limits on large-scale training. The relocated resolution plot loses v1's explicit qualification that adaptability covers resolutions used during training.

D1.justification: v2 removes the detailed decoder diagram and its GELU specification, together with the stated 16-dimensional ground-plane embedding size. Main-text ground-plane embedding remains, as do most hyperparameters, hardware information, dataset splits, and calibration instructions. The project website address also changes.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against GEDepth, GroCo, and PlaneDepth through Appendix G's detailed critique of their generalization mechanisms and convergence. It also adds MOFT and removes the RA-Depth and GELU references; other citation-number changes largely reflect renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 adds contribution bullets, rewrites the conclusion and selected explanations, and reorganizes material between the main text and supplements. Resolution discussion moves into the main text; qualitative and fusion ablations move into supplementary sections. Most existing method and experimental prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 restructures the ground-plane comparison tables, adds a surround-view table and a comparator schematic, expands Figure 6 with GEDepth bars, and removes the decoder diagram. Resolution, qualitative-ablation, and fusion displays move between the main text and supplements, substantially changing presentation.

improvement.justification: Matched GEDepth comparisons and the supervised PlaneDepth control strengthen evidence that generalization differences extend beyond supervision and model complexity; surround-view tests broaden validation. These gains are tempered by lost decoder details and new reporting inconsistencies: Table 4 duplicates a side-view heading, and Tables 3 and 5 disagree on some repeated Vertical scores, including DrivingStereo-to-DDAD A.Rel of 14.71 versus 15.71.
